overview: The images-to-PDF converter combines photos, scans and screenshots into a single PDF. Add up to 100 images, drag them into the order you want, choose a page size and margins, and download the finished document. Everything is assembled in your browser.

Page layout has three options. A4 uses the standard 210 × 297 mm page, US Letter uses 8.5 × 11 inches, and Fit-to-image makes every page exactly as large as its picture. Orientation can follow each image automatically or force portrait or landscape. The margin option adds 24 points or 48 points of white space around the image, where 72 points equal one inch, so 24 points is about 8.5 mm and 48 points about 17 mm.

Each image is scaled to fit inside the printable area without distortion, which means an image whose aspect ratio differs from the page will be centred with blank space rather than stretched. Transparent PNGs are converted with a background, and very large photos are re-encoded to keep the resulting PDF manageable. The original image files are never modified.
useCases: Turn a set of scanned receipts or ID documents into one PDF.
Assemble photographed pages into a single submission file.
Combine screenshots into a report appendix.
Create a simple photo portfolio or lookbook.
Convert whiteboard photos into a shareable document.
images-to-pdf.workedExample: Add six phone photos and drag them into reading order. Choose A4, portrait orientation and a 24-point margin. A landscape photo is scaled until its width fits the printable area and is centred vertically, leaving white space above and below; a portrait photo fills more of the page. The output is a six-page PDF named whatever you type in the filename field, with one image per page and no distortion of the originals.
limits: Up to 100 images per document, each no larger than 20 MB. Unsupported formats are skipped.
Images are fitted to the page rather than cropped to fill it, so mixed aspect ratios leave white space.
Text in the images is not recognised, and the PDF contains no searchable text layer unless the source images already include one.
Very large photos are re-encoded, which can slightly reduce detail, and the PDF is generated in memory, so extremely large batches may be slow on low-memory devices.
images-to-pdf.privacy: Images and the generated PDF stay on your device. The PDF library is downloaded from a public CDN, but no image content is uploaded to ToolNova or the CDN.

faq.a: Yes. Drag the image thumbnails into the order you want before pressing Create PDF.

faq.q: Which page size should I choose?
faq.a: A4 for most of the world, US Letter for North America, or Fit-to-image when the page must match the picture exactly.
Only if the images contain a text layer already. This tool places images on pages; it does not run optical character recognition.

overview: The PDF merger joins two or more PDF files into a single document. Add up to 50 files of up to 50 MB each, arrange them in the order you want, and download the combined PDF. Pages keep their original content, orientation and bookmarks where the underlying library preserves them.

Order matters: the merger copies the pages of each file in the sequence shown in the list, so the first file's pages come first. Drag the entries to reorder them before merging. The output is a new file; the originals are not altered, which means you can experiment freely and still keep the source documents.

Merging is useful for combining signed contracts, invoice batches, scanned forms or chapters that were exported separately. It is a page-level operation, not a document-management system: it does not fill forms, compress images, remove passwords or repair damaged files. If a source PDF is encrypted or malformed, the merger will report that it cannot read it.
useCases: Combine several signed pages into one contract PDF.
Join monthly statements or invoices into a single archive file.
Assemble separately scanned chapters into one document.
Merge a cover letter and its attachments before emailing.
Put a cover page in front of an existing report.
pdf-merger.workedExample: Suppose you have a two-page cover letter, a five-page proposal and a one-page signature sheet. Add them in that order and press Merge. The result is an eight-page PDF whose first two pages come from the letter, pages three to seven from the proposal and page eight from the signature sheet. If you drag the signature sheet to the top instead, it becomes page one and the letter shifts to pages two and three.
limits: Up to 50 files and 50 MB per file. Encrypted or password-protected PDFs cannot be merged unless they are unlocked first.
Form fields, digital signatures and interactive features may not survive the copy, and existing signatures are invalidated by any change to the document.
The merged file is held in memory while it is built, so very large batches can be slow or fail on devices with limited RAM.
No compression is applied; the output size is roughly the sum of the input sizes plus a small overhead.
pdf-merger.privacy: The PDFs are read and combined locally in your browser. The PDF library is loaded from a public CDN, but the documents themselves are never uploaded.

faq.a: No. Pages are copied rather than re-rendered, so text and images keep their original quality. The file size is approximately the sum of the sources.
Not directly. Remove the password with the owner's permission first, then merge the unlocked copies.

faq.q: Will bookmarks and links be preserved?
faq.a: Page content is preserved, but annotations, bookmarks and internal links may be dropped or need adjustment depending on the source files.

overview: The rotate PDF tool turns pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. You can rotate the whole document, only odd pages, only even pages, or a custom list such as 1-3, 5, 8-10. The rotation is added to each page's existing orientation, so running the tool twice by 90 degrees produces a 180-degree result.

Rotating scanned pages is a common fix after a sheet is fed sideways or upside down. The tool changes the page's rotation attribute rather than re-rendering the content, so text stays sharp and the file does not lose quality. A fresh copy of the document is loaded for each run, which prevents repeated runs from stacking rotations unintentionally.

The tool works on one PDF at a time and does not modify the original file on disk. It downloads a new copy with a filename based on the original, so you can compare the corrected version with the source before replacing anything.
useCases: Fix a scanned page that was fed sideways.
Rotate only landscape pages in a mixed-orientation document.
Turn an upside-down scan by 180 degrees.
Correct a custom set of pages without affecting the rest.
Prepare a document for on-screen reading after a mobile scan.
rotate-pdf.workedExample: A 12-page scan has pages 4 and 5 upside down. Choose Custom, enter 4-5 and select 180 degrees. The tool loads the PDF, adds 180 degrees to the rotation of those two pages and leaves the other ten untouched. The downloaded file still has 12 pages, but pages 4 and 5 now display the right way up; running the same operation again would return them to upside down because the rotation is cumulative.
limits: One file at a time. Batch rotation across several PDFs must be done one after another.
Encrypted or damaged PDFs cannot be processed until they are unlocked or repaired.
The tool changes page rotation metadata, not the orientation of content that was scanned sideways within a correctly oriented page.
Rotating a page that contains a digital signature invalidates that signature, as with any modification.
rotate-pdf.privacy: The document is opened and modified on your device. The PDF library is fetched from a CDN, but the file's contents are never uploaded.

faq.a: The new file stores the rotated orientation. Repeating the operation adds to it, so two 90-degree runs equal 180 degrees.

faq.q: Can I rotate only the pages that are sideways?
faq.a: Yes. Use the Custom scope and list the page numbers or ranges. There is no automatic detection of sideways content.
Yes. The page content is not re-rendered; only its rotation attribute changes, so vector text and images remain intact.

overview: The split PDF tool extracts pages from a document in three ways. Extract mode pulls the pages you list into one PDF. Ranges mode creates a separate PDF for each range. Each-page mode turns every page into its own file. Page numbers are one-based, and ranges such as 3-7 are inclusive.

The output is generated from the original file without re-rendering, so text and images keep their quality. In Extract mode, the selected pages are concatenated in the order you list them, which means you can also use it to reorder a subset. In Ranges mode, the output names include the range, and in Each-page mode they include a padded page number.

Splitting is handy for pulling an invoice out of a statement, separating chapters, or producing individual handouts from a slide deck. It does not remove passwords, compress images or merge documents; use the dedicated tools for those jobs. Damaged or encrypted PDFs must be repaired or unlocked before splitting.
useCases: Extract a single invoice or receipt from a monthly statement.
Split a long report into one file per chapter.
Create individual handouts from a slide deck.
Pull a page range into its own document for review.
Reorder a subset of pages by listing them in the desired order.
split-pdf.workedExample: A 24-page report needs pages 2-4 and page 10 as a single handout. Choose Extract, enter "2-4, 10" and split. The result is a four-page PDF containing pages 2, 3, 4 and 10 in that order. Switching to Ranges with the same input produces two files, one with pages 2-4 and one with page 10. Each-page mode ignores the page field and produces 24 separate single-page PDFs.
limits: One source file at a time. Splitting several PDFs requires repeating the operation.
Encrypted or malformed PDFs cannot be split until they are unlocked or repaired.
Bookmarks, annotations and form fields may be lost or need rework in the extracted copies.
Each-page mode on a very long document produces many downloads, which some browsers block unless you allow multiple downloads.
split-pdf.privacy: The PDF is processed locally. The library is downloaded from a CDN, but the document's pages are never uploaded to ToolNova or the CDN.

faq.q: Does Extract merge ranges into one file?
faq.a: Yes. Extract combines every page you list into a single PDF, in the order given. Use Ranges when you want a separate file per range.
No. Page 1 is the first page, and ranges such as 3-7 include both endpoints.

faq.q: Why did only one file download?
faq.a: In Each-page or Ranges mode the browser may block multiple automatic downloads. Allow multiple downloads for the site and run the split again.
